From: Mark Atwood <mark@reviewcommit.com>
To: René Cordier <rcordier@linagora.com>
Subject: draft-atwood-jmap-updates-00 updates RFC 9425 (Quota description language)

Hi René,

I wanted to tell you directly that my new draft,
draft-atwood-jmap-updates-00 (LIST-THREAD-URL), lists "Updates: 9425".
The change is narrow and applies only to clients that opt in to its
capability:

- Quota name and description become localizable: a base value with a
  `locale`, plus per-language `localizations`.
- For those clients, a `language` argument on Quota/get replaces
  selection of the description by Accept-Language (9425 Section 4.1).
  The reason is that if the data changes with a request header, a
  client's state-keyed cache can end up mixing languages.

Clients that don't opt in see exactly the RFC 9425 behaviour. Does
this look right to you, and is there anything about how servers
generate the description in practice that I should account for?

Thanks,
Mark

  selection of the description by Accept-Language (9425 Section 4.1).
  The reason is that if the data changes with a request header, a
  client's state-keyed cache can end up mixing languages.
